subject: Post-demo model shortlist and decision checklist
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zephyrus.ai>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@zephyrus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo model shortlist and decision checklist

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid feedback and the clear priorities you shared (latency < 120ms p95, tight cost targets for scale, and zero-PHI policy). Quickly capturing what we discussed and the recommended next steps so we have a single decision checklist for the team.

Quick recap of the demo takeaways:
- Primary workload: user-facing summarization + short-form Q&A (~128 token outputs, 1–3 prompt turns).
- SLOs: p95 latency <= 120ms in US-West, target throughput 120 rps sustained.
- Constraints: no user data leaves VPC; audit logs required for production.

Redwood initial recommended shortlist (balanced by cost / latency / quality):
1) redwood-llm-medium-q4 (quantized FP16 profile) — Best baseline for cost-sensitive scale. Expected token cost lowest, p95 latency ~90–110ms on dedicated c6g-class instances, good if you accept modest drop on complex summarization edge-cases.
2) open-transformer-s-xl (float16) — Highest raw quality on abstractive summaries, p95 latency ~130–160ms on same infra; recommend for premium tier where fidelity matters.
3) editor-lite-8b (8B int8) — Sweet spot for predictable latency (<100ms after prefix caching) with strong extraction precision; recommended when strict latency SLOs trump marginal quality gains.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- We will run a focused eval on your canonical prompt set (please see attached prompt-sets-v1.jsonl). Expected output: per-prompt ROUGE/BLEU-like metrics + qualitative notes. Target deliverable by 48–72 hours.
- Internal: Marissa will run the latency/cost profiling and share the raw CSV (zeph-demo-benchmarks.csv).
- Procurement: Olga to share a mutual action plan + draft SOW for initial POC (attached).

Risks we flagged during the call:
- Potential quality regressions on long-context corner cases — we'll add targeted tests.
- VPC private deployment timeline depends on your security review; SOC2 evidence requested (if you need it now, say the word).

If this checklist matches your read, reply with which model you want prioritized for the POC evaluation (we can run 1 primary + 1 fallback in parallel).

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zephyrus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@zephyrus.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist and decision checklist

Thanks, Olga — this is great and super actionable. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we pick a primary: 
1) For the redwood-llm-medium-q4 profile, do you have a ballpark monthly cost estimate at our expected 120 rps sustained (we're estimating ~26M tokens/mo)?
2) For the open-transformer-s-xl, is there an option to run a lower-latency variant (e.g., 1-2 token caching optimizations) for the most frequent short queries?

Tom and I prefer starting with the cheapest reasonable option (redwood-llm-medium-q4) but we want to make sure we aren't sacrificing critical summary fidelity. Also -- can you share the evaluation rubric you'll use?

Best,
Laura
Director of Product, Zephyrus Analytics
laura.chen@zephyrus.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zephyrus.ai>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@zephyrus.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist and decision checklist — bench + rubric

Laura — quick answers inline and attaching the eval artifacts.

> For the redwood-llm-medium-q4 profile, do you have a ballpark monthly cost estimate at our expected 120 rps sustained (we're estimating ~26M tokens/mo)?
- See zeph-demo-benchmarks.csv (attached): baseline run (no caching) suggests ~0.8 USD per 1k tokens for medium-q4 on Dedicated c6g pools. At 26M tokens/mo that's ~20.8k USD/mo in raw token costs; with batching and prefix caching we typically see 20–30% reduction depending on request distribution.

> open-transformer-s-xl lower-latency variant?
- There is a float16 runtime profile optimized for prefix caching; in our internal runs p95 dropped from ~150ms to ~120ms but cost increased ~25% due to larger instance footprint. We'll include that specific run in the attached CSV and the eval run link below.

Attached evaluation artifacts:
- zeph-demo-benchmarks.csv — per-model latency distribution + per-token cost estimate (columns: model, profile, p50,p95,p99, cost_per_1k_tokens).
- prompt-sets-v1.jsonl — canonical prompt set you gave us (sanitized) plus a few edge-case prompts we added to stress-test abstraction.
- mvp-mutual-action-plan.pdf — proposed timeline / milestones for a 4-week POC.

Evaluation rubric (short):
- Quality: ROUGE-L, embedding-similarity to human reference, 30 manual spot-checks for hallucination rate.
- Latency: p95 measured under 120 rps synthetic and a production-like mixed workload.
- Cost: projected monthly token cost + infra amortized (per-run numbers in CSV).
- Regression gates: any model that shows >= 5% drop in key quality metric on your canonical prompts will not be promoted without manual review.

We kicked off the eval run here: https://app.redwoodinference.com/evals/run/9876 (results tab populated — open to your team). Based on the first pass, our suggested primary/fallback for the POC: primary = redwood-llm-medium-q4, fallback = editor-lite-8b. We'll keep open-transformer-s-xl as an elevated option if you want highest-fidelity tier later.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist and decision checklist — internal ask + next actions

Looping you both in to align on the procurement ask and the POC scoping. Action items I recommend so we can move to DocuSign this week: 
1) Rishi: can you produce a one-page pricing table for ZD-2027-0017 with three tiers (POC - 1mo term, POC committed 3mo, Production annual commit) showing: model (primary/fallback), per-1k token price, monthly committed commit discount, and estimated infra cost per 100k tokens? Need this by EOD tomorrow.
2) Marissa: finalize the POC eval run notes and lock the eval gate: any model with >=5% regression on canonical prompts gets flagged. Please attach the final CSV and a short executive one-pager for procurement (2 slides max).
3) Olga (me): I'll drop the SOW skeleton into the Drive folder and share a DocuSign link once Rishi confirm pricing. Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-zephyrus-eval  — I placed the current draft under /SOW/draft_v1.docx.

Model recommendation for the pricing table: primary = redwood-llm-medium-q4, fallback = editor-lite-8b. If procurement asks for an SLA exception for the pilot, offer a narrow SLA that covers regional uptime but excludes degradations caused by customer-managed VPC/networking during onboarding.

I'll update the HubSpot deal with these next steps (link: https://crm.hubspot.com/deal/ZD-2027-0017) and follow up with a DocuSign invite.

—
Olga Petrov
